turns.speaker: unknown
turns.text: Ridgeway Motor Group / Invoca | escalation | Tue, Oct 20, 2026

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Morning everyone. Thanks for making time. [PERSON_1], [PERSON_2], I've got [PERSON_3] here from our support escalations team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Morning. I've read the ticket notes, so I have some background, but I'd rather hear it from you directly.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Appreciate you both getting on. Let's cut to it, because I've got a store to run.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: So, quick version. Our Google Ads call conversions have been at least two days behind since the middle of September. Our cost per appointment is up about forty percent.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Forty percent. On a budget that size, that's real money every week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. When you say two days behind, is that the timestamp on the conversion in Google Ads versus when the call happened here?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Right. Our BDC marks the appointment in Salesforce, and the call itself was two days earlier. So Google's seeing the conversion late, and Smart Bidding is reacting late.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Got it. And that's your whole paid search budget, or a subset of campaigns?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Seven campaigns, basically everything with a tracking number. It's not one bad campaign.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Did the delay start all at once, or creep up on you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Creep. First it was a few hours off, then a day, now it's two plus. The week of September 14th is when I first flagged it internally.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And it's still going. That's the part that burns me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Can you walk me through what happens on your end between the call and the conversion landing in Google Ads?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The call comes in, it shows up as a call activity in Salesforce on the lead, our BDC marks the appointment outcome, and that outcome is what we're sending to Google as the offline conversion.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Thanks. And who made the connection between the call and the lead on the Salesforce side, was that you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I set up the mapping back in March with help from your team, and it worked fine through the summer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Okay. And you haven't changed the Salesforce side recently, no new fields or workflows?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Not that I know of. I can pull a change log if that helps.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Please. Send it to me directly. And the timestamps you're seeing, are those from the Google Ads UI or from a report?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Both, actually. I pulled the conversion report and cross-checked against the UI. Same delay.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: And nothing's changed on the Google Ads side, no new conversion actions or account changes?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Our marketing coordinator handles that. I'll confirm with him today, but he says he hasn't touched anything.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Let me jump in here, because I want to be straight with you. I came in as GM in August, and I inherited a stack of vendor contracts I didn't sign.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Understood.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Marchex says they'll match whatever we're paying and throw in the first three months free.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. I'd rather hear that now than later, so thank you for saying it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I'd rather not switch. It's work for my team. But I've got thirty days to show my owner this is fixed, or I'm moving us to Marchex. That's not a negotiating tactic.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Fair enough. What would good look like for you in thirty days?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Conversions landing same day. Not perfect, same day. If I can't tell my owner the numbers are clean by then, I'm done defending it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Same day would get us back to where we were in July.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Give me the change log, the conversion report export, and a handful of example calls with the lead IDs. I'll take it to the team that owns the sending pipeline.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I can have all of that over by end of day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Then you'll hear from me tomorrow, one way or the other. If I don't have a root cause yet, I'll tell you exactly what we've ruled out and what we're testing next.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: A daily note beats a status update a week out, I'll tell you that.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I'll coordinate on my side so [PERSON_3] has whatever he needs from your account, and I'll join the next update.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Fine. And just so nobody's surprised, I've asked my controller to put together a comparison sheet this week. That's due diligence, not a decision.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: That's your call to make. Our job right now is to get you an answer on this.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: One more question, [PERSON_2]. When the conversion finally lands, does the original call timestamp stay intact, or does it get rewritten to the send date?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The timestamp on the call is fine. It's the arrival in Google that's late.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good, that narrows it. I'll stop guessing until I see the data.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Then let's not burn more time on this call. [PERSON_2], get him the files.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: On it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Thanks, both. [PERSON_3], I'll set up the shared folder after this.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Sounds good. [PERSON_1], [PERSON_2], talk tomorrow.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Tomorrow. Thanks.
